newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni captors free seven Germans - security source.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni captors free seven Germans - security source.

text.p: Seven German tourists held hostage by Yemeni tribesmen in the southeastern province of Hadramaut were freed on Wednesday, a senior security source said.
"The seven were freed hours ago and are now in Rayyan airport in Mukalla city in Hadramaut waiting to board a special Yemeni plane that will take them to Sanaa en route to Germany," he told Reuters.
He could not say when the tourists would be flown back home. Other officials were not available for comment.
The kidnappers on Tuesday changed their minds at the last minute about releasing them after holding them for a week. Talks on their freedom later resumed.
The seven men, aged between 30 and 45, were kidnapped while riding morotcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area, some 770 km (480 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
Kidnapping is a common ploy in Yemen by tribesmen holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms.
President Ali Abdullah Saleh personally followed up on developments related to the hostage saga.

A Yemeni security official said on Tuesday last-minute negotiations centred on the tribesmen's demand of a government amnesty in return for releasing their hostages. The official declined to say whether any of the demands had been met.
Dozens of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners have been seized in recent years in Yemen, one of the Arab world's most impoverished states.
The tribesmen have tried to use the foreigners, who have included a U.S. diplomat and a Saudi ambassador, as bargaining chips.
Siege by security forces has been the usual government response.
In the latest incident, the tribesmen wanted to pressure the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them cars smuggled from Gulf Arab states.
